name: Clear the Copilot review findings carried by the open PR stack
description:
Copilot left 33 review threads across the open addon-reviewer stack. Each was re-read against its own PR head rather than trusted on GitHub's "outdated" flag — that flag only says the diff hunk moved, not that anything was fixed. Fifteen turned out to be genuinely fixed and are closed. Six were examined and are not being taken (see the appendix). The remaining eleven are real and collected here.

**Deliberately not fixed in the PRs they were raised on.** The stack is twelve deep — PR 29 is the base for 31 → 32 → 33 → 37 → 40 → 42 → 43 → 44 → 61 → 62/64 — so a fix near the bottom means rebasing the whole chain, and a migration mid-stack means renumbering the drizzle files, which has already cost us once. All of this is done in one pass against `master` after the open PRs are merged.

Two of the eleven had a choice to make; both are decided below and the estimates assume the decision.

## Partner-visible

### 1. A re-run deletes the rows a published canonical points at

`packages/runner/src/run-review.ts`, the crash-re-entry cleanup.

The cleanup deletes this review's comments scoped to `unpublishedComment()`, which is `published_at IS NULL`. Covered engine rows carry exactly that: a release publishes the canonical as the unit, so only the canonical id lands in `published_comment_ids` and the engine rows it consolidates stay unpublished by design — `finding-rounds.ts` says so out loud ("filtering them by publication would empty every canonical's identity"). Requeueing that engine review therefore deletes them while the already-published canonical still holds their ids in `covers`.

Both routes to recognising the finding die together. `listOpenFindingsForPr` finds no locations for the canonical and marks it `neverResolvable`, so identity cannot match it; and `continues_comment_id` is declared `onDelete: "set null"`, so the link route is nulled by the same delete. The next round posts a second thread for a problem the partner already has open — the exact failure the dedup work exists to prevent — and the loss is permanent.

Reachable through an ordinary requeue from the console, which is what PR 52 and PR 54 are both about.

**Fix:** narrow the delete so a row covered by a published canonical survives it (a `where not exists` over published judge rows' `covers`), or repoint those rows before deleting. Roughly half a day; the cost is the jsonb containment query and a test that reproduces release → requeue.

### 2. Fence-token sanitising does not cover every renderer

`packages/runner/src/prompt.ts`.

`FENCE_TOKENS` is applied only through `sanitizeTitle`/`sanitizeBlock`. `renderSupplyChain` interpolates its values raw although its own docblock states that package names and script URLs are attacker-controlled, and `renderReplyDraftFinding` does the same with `body`, `fix` and `verify`. An npm package name cannot carry the tokens (they are upper-case), but a remote script URL, a path in `lockfilesTouched` and the `flags` list all can, and a value carrying the active closing token ends the fence early. The hardening claim made in PR 32 is therefore not true of the whole prompt surface.

**Fix:** route those fields through the existing sanitisers — about eight interpolation sites across the two renderers, plus a test per renderer. One to two hours.

### 3. `sameProblem` matches two null rule codes

`packages/github/src/draft.ts`.

For a pathful finding where both sides carry a fingerprint, the last condition is `candidate.ruleCode === open.ruleCode`, so `null === null` counts two findings as the same problem. The `PublishCandidate` contract in the same file says the opposite: NULL "is normal (a pre-classification round, a provider that emits no rule codes, a judge canonical, an unreadable file) and never matches; the fallback in `crossRoundSuppressed` is what answers for those."

**Decision: the code stays, the contract is corrected.** The `sameProblem` docblock already argues the trade deliberately — a duplicate thread is the worse failure, and the same trade is stated as a rule one step over in reconcile — so the behaviour is intended and the contract sentence is the thing that is wrong. Tightening the code instead would publish more claudecode findings today and would be a behaviour change smuggled in as a comment fix.

Note this is the same root as CZ3TDR1-725: the collision only bites for a provider that emits no rule codes, which today is claudecode. Two findings on one line from that provider share a fingerprint and a path, and one gets suppressed. Once 725 lands the collision stops being reachable; until then the contract should describe what the code does. Two to four hours, almost all of it the docblock.

## Operator- and correctness-facing

### 4. The sticky bar overstates what a release sends

`apps/console/app/review/[id]/review-sticky-bar.tsx`.

Copilot pointed at the Section header in `pr-review.tsx`; that caller was fixed and now goes through `goingOutCount`. A sweep found the same bug one file over: the "Release N comments" button still computes `rows.filter((r) => r.included).length`, so a carried-over row that is held back is still counted. `goingOutCount`'s own docblock claims the count is "the only place the two questions meet, and the only place that can get it wrong", which stopped being true. Fifteen minutes.

### 5. The outbound admin help contradicts the defaults it documents

`apps/console/app/admin/outbound/outbound-admin.tsx` vs `packages/db/src/policies.ts`.

`defaultModeFor` returns `gated` for the four `finding_*` events plus `findings_release`, `reply` and `command_ack` — seven. The Czech help text still says gated is the default for six of ten and lists command acknowledgements among the events that stay off. Operators are shown the opposite of what the code does. Twenty minutes, text only.

### 6. A database write error is reported as a GitHub read failure

`apps/worker/src/jobs/reconcile-findings.ts`, the thread-state block.

`persistThreadState` sits inside the same `try` as the GitHub read, and the `catch` logs "thread-state read failed; classifying on the stored columns". A failed write is therefore treated as stale-but-usable thread state, classification continues on it, and the error is never retried although the job's own docstring says it should be. Copilot listed four more line numbers; they have since moved, and a sweep confirms every other failure path in the file is a narrow `.catch()` on one promise, so this is the last broad one.

**Fix:** take the write out of the guarded region so a DB error escapes. One to two hours including a test for each direction.

### 7. A failed reconcile enqueue is lost silently

`apps/worker/src/jobs/review-pr.ts`, `maybeEnqueueReconcile`.

The catch logs a warning and returns. For a single-scout head, or when the final judge settle is the one that throws, this is the only trigger, so that head is never classified and the once-per-round guarantee is quietly broken.

The docblock already wrote up why the cheap guard does not work: `pr_snapshots.reconciled_at` is stamped on every exit, so it means "a run finished here", not "this head is done". An honest fix needs a second signal or a new column plus a sweep, which is one to two days including a migration.

**Proposed as the proportionate answer:** raise the failure to a Slack alert instead of `log.warn`, so it stops being silent, and leave a TODO for the sweep. About an hour. Reassess if it ever fires.

### 8. `/rereview` answers "fresh" for a head that can never get a live row

`packages/db/src/reviews-write.ts`, `headFullyReviewed`.

`headFullyReviewed` excludes `origin: 'backfill'`, so a head whose only rows are backfill-origin reads as not-yet-reviewed. Triage then cannot create the live row: `reviewExists` queries only repo, PR, head and provider and never looks at `origin`, and the unique index `reviews_repo_pr_head_provider_uq` blocks the replacement. The head can be enqueued repeatedly while nothing partner-visible ever appears.

Reachability is narrow — `backfill-repo.ts` enumerates closed PRs only, so it needs a backfilled PR that was reopened and then commented on.

**Decision: the cheap variant.** Refuse `/rereview` on such a head with a clear answer rather than making `reviewExists` origin-aware and changing the unique index, which would mean a migration for a case this rare. Half a day.

### 9. The `claimReview` docblock claims more than supersede does

`packages/db/src/reviews-write.ts`.

It says an older head's rows are never touched because each is "either terminal (decided) or was superseded while still open". `supersedeOpenPriorReviews` only stamps `queued`, `running`, `pending` and `approved`, so a `failed` or `rejected` row on an older head is neither, and `prRowsWhere` filters only on head and `superseded_at` — so it can be claimed.

Worth doing together with the neighbouring text: PR 52's docblock on `supersedeOpenPriorReviews` describes this same fact correctly and at length, so the two files currently contradict each other. Half an hour.

### 10. The stale-head requeue guard is not atomic with the transition

`apps/console/lib/actions.ts` and `assertHeadNotStale`.

`assertHeadNotStale` reads, then `transition` writes. A poll landing in between runs `supersedeOpenPriorReviews` while the row is still `rejected` — which excludes it from the stamp — and inserts the new head's rows; the action then moves the old row to `queued` and enqueues it against stale code, unsuperseded, so `outbound-send`'s `if (review.supersededAt)` check passes. Narrow window, but it reopens exactly the path PR 54 exists to close. Copilot raised it from both sides; it is one issue.

**Fix:** put the guard read and the transition in one `db.transaction` with the review row locked, keeping the enqueue outside it. `engine-logins.ts` has the transaction pattern; there is no row-lock helper yet. Three to five hours, mostly the interleaving test.

### 11. An oversized blob throws where the contract promises null

`packages/github/src/ref-source.ts`.

`RefReadSource`'s own contract says both reads answer `null` where the answer is "we cannot know", because a read that throws would fail the round. The catch rethrows everything but a 404, and the Contents API answers 403 for blobs over 100 MB — so the size guard below it is never reached and the reconcile aborts instead of degrading to "still open".

**Fix:** recognise the too-large response and return null while still rethrowing authentication failures. `isRateLimited` in `outbound-poster.ts` is the shape to copy. One to two hours.

_Sequencing note:_ this one sits at the bottom of the stack. Even after the merge it is worth keeping in its own change rather than bundled, since it is the least urgent of the eleven.

## Batching

Items 1, 3 and 4 are all in the PR 37 area; 6 and 7 in PR 33's; 5 and 8 in PR 40's. One pass per area rather than one per item is what keeps the whole set near three days rather than four.

## Appendix — examined and not taken

- `finding-diff.ts` zero-context insertion (PR 32) — the code already carries the case, the worked example and the argument that GitHub's compare always sends context, with the failure direction documented as safe.
- `normalizeSignal` on URLs (PR 29) — real collapsing of distinct ids, but named as intent in the docblock, and it errs toward keeping a finding open.
- `reconcile_dry_run` has no console control (PR 33) — Copilot offered "add the control or document the path"; `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` carries a runnable SQL upsert and CLAUDE.md names the switch.
- `supersedeOpenPriorReviews` docblock overreach on requeue (PR 52) — "all the way to published" holds for engine rows only, since `requeueReviewAction` routes by `reviewQueueKind` and publishing is gated by `publishEnabled`. Cosmetic; fold into item 9 if that text is being touched anyway.
- `gt` vs `gte` on `created_at` (PR 54) — premise does not hold. The file documents shared timestamps for rows inserted in one transaction; the old row and a newer head's rows are always separate transactions, so the tie cannot occur.
- Non-array `coversCommentIds` (PR 31) — refuted. The verdict parser reduces `covers` to `null | string[]` and has a test for it, judge-pr maps every element through `resolveRef`, and the consuming docblock states that contract explicitly. The column is new, so there is no legacy data behind it either.

**Done when:** each of the eleven is fixed or, where the ticket records a decision, resolved the way the decision says; the contract in `draft.ts` describes what `sameProblem` actually does; `/rereview` gives a straight answer on a backfill-only head instead of looping; and no release count, admin help text or docblock in the set still claims more than the code does.
